evidence:
The literal copying premise is verified, but check (d), materiality, refutes this as a review defect. At the frozen tip, src/store/invitation_content.rs:289-415 reads all private State fields and copies them into serde values; :473-520 serializes/clones them for a full upsert. refresh() calls these at :2945 and :3080. render_selection() at :600-638 needs only frozen identity, but performs the same full read; service/delivery_presentation.rs:137-139 calls it for admission, store/invitation_content.rs:2127 rechecks it inside the deciding transaction, and :2170 loads State again. service/mod_channels.rs:355-469 invokes refresh for admitted capable bindings, and store/mod.rs:1231-1245 takes the writer decision. Thus this is a valid possible optimization, not an invented observation.
(a) Present under another name: src/store/presentation_reader.rs:106-158 already uses narrow scope/counter SELECT and guarded UPDATE for canonical reader invalidation. It does not replace refresh or render_selection, so it does not falsify the literal premise. Its narrower required envelope belongs specifically to reader-operation invalidation (TRUST-POLICY.md:1821-1845; resume-v090-q4-direct-lazy-reader-episode-design.md:90-92), not every State accessor.
(b) Stated contract: Q3 R7 (resume-v090-q3-channel-design.md:20) preserves existing numeric work/output/storage envelopes. TRUST-POLICY.md:1544-1554 expressly chooses two fixed consumer rows per used binding and permits binding history to multiply retained rows. :1572-1582 accepts partial/carry byte ceilings. Migration0044_invitation_presentation.sql:68-83 and load_raw():315-350 bound the four cited large fields to 155731/49415/262144/65536 bytes (sum532826; this is a loose sum of individual caps, not proof that all maxima are jointly produced). Ancillary strings also have explicit checked bounds. There is no contract requiring metadata-only column reads or prohibiting a byte-preserving full upsert. I found no explicit acceptance of the extra copying itself, so I do not pretend that storage bounds alone prove it desirable.
(c) Scope: this is one fixed keyed row per addressed consumer, not a scan of all retained presentation payloads. The worker's active registry is capped at64 (src/protocol/watch.rs:71; src/service/mod_channels.rs:204,845); entries are processed sequentially (:391). src/service/workers.rs:1146-1180 performs the quiet safety pass every10 one-second ticks, with additional dirty passes. Therefore unbounded-retention scaling or an unlimited-channel premise would exceed the actual execution envelope. Narrow accessors remain within scope as an optional optimization.
(d) Materiality/pragmatism: the finding explicitly disclaims a measured wall-clock breach, and establishes no incorrect delivery, lost state, extra logical offer, frontiers changed by passive refresh, unbounded source walk, or exceeded numeric allowance. The contract expressly distinguishes source accounting from elapsed-time/disk-I/O guarantees (TRUST-POLICY.md:1858-1866). The original State is loaded and written within the writer decision, so the full upsert preserves unrelated payload values rather than creating a lost-update example. Fixed bounded copies and extra validation may cost work, but their existence alone does not demonstrate significant risk, rework, or a changed required outcome. Narrow SELECT/UPDATE accessors are a plausible improvement requiring preservation of scope/counter/corruption checks; they are not a missing contract mechanism. Deferred final measurements remain required and are not treated as passed. A demonstrated budget regression or prohibited payload mutation would be a different actionable finding.
(e) Pre-existing: git ls-tree of base565def86 has neither invitation_content.rs nor presentation_reader.rs; the diff introduces them (+3094/+164). Base service/mod_channels.rs:332-409 uses only mod_binding_view and never performs this new refresh, so the literal coupling is new, not a pre-existing defect classified FYI.
(f) Linter territory: this is structural allocation/SQL behavior, not formatting or a lint-enforced rule; this check does not refute it. No external/library-performance premise is needed for this verdict. Rejected because materiality is not demonstrated against the stated bounded contract, not because the code lacks the described copies.
